question.text: A wheel of radius R and mass M is placed at the bottom of a fixed step of height R as shown in the figure. A constant force is continuously applied on the surface of the wheel so that it just climbs the step without slipping. Consider the torque τ about an axis normal to the plane of the paper passing through the point Q. Which of the following options is/are correct?

options.text: If the force is applied normal to the circumference at point  <math><mi>X</mi></math>  then  <math><mi>τ</mi></math>  is constant
If the force is applied tangentially at point S then  <math><mi>τ</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>  but the wheel never climbs the step
If the force is applied normal to the circumference at point P then <math><mi>τ</mi></math> is zero
If the force is applied at point P tangentially then  <math><mi>τ</mi></math>  decreases continuously as the wheel climbs

solution.text:
(i) is incorrect.

If force is applied normal to surface at point X

τ=Fy Rsin⁡θ

Thus τ depends on θ and it is not constant

(ii) is incorrect

If force applied tangentially at S

τ=F×R ≠0

But it will climb as mentioned in question.

If force is applied normal to surface at P then line of action of force will pass from Q and thus τ=0

(iv) is incorrect.

If force is applied at P tangentially the τ=F×2R=constant
